en: The Sutra of the Five Mothers and Sons, translated by the Wu-period Upāsaka Zhi Qian.
Formerly, there was an Arhat dwelling in the mountains who practiced the prohibitions of the Way. There was a small...

At the age of seven, the boy took a great liking to the Way; he left his home to become a śramaṇa, followed his teacher into the mountains, and studied the Dharma under him with diligent and tireless effort.
At the age of eight, he attained four supernatural powers:

first, his eyes could see through all things; second, his ears could hear through all things; third, he was able to fly and manifest transformations; and fourth, he knew his own past lives and the origins from which he had come.
As he sat in contemplation, he immediately perceived his past lives and the experiences he had undergone, having been the son of five different mothers.
At that moment, he smiled to himself.
His teacher asked him:
"Why do you smile? Here in the mountains there are no entertainers, nor singing or dancing; for what reason do you smile?
The śrāmaṇera said:
"I did not dare to laugh at my teacher.

When I look upon myself, I see that I have five mothers who all weep and wail for me day and night; moved by grief and tormented by sorrow, they constantly speak of and think of their son, never having forgotten him for even a moment."
I thought to myself that my own single body was afflicted by the suffering of the five families; for this reason, I laughed, not daring to laugh at the Teacher.
"When I was the child of my first mother, there was a neighbor who was born at the same time as I."
After my death, on the same day someone else was born, that person began to walk about; when my mother saw this, she said:
"If my son were still alive, he too would be walking about!"
Thus, she was filled with grief and sorrow, feeling deep pain as she thought of me.
Furthermore, I became her second son; not long after I was born, I died again.
When my mother saw others nursing their children with milk, she felt such poignant pain thinking of me that she grieved and wept for me.
"Furthermore, he became the son of my third mother, but he died again before long.
As my mother was about to eat, tears fell from her eyes as she thought of me, saying:
'If you were still alive, you would be eating with me.'"
“May he abandon me and pass away!
Thus she grieved and worried for me.
Furthermore, I became the son of a fourth mother, but before long, I died again.
When my peers of the same age were taking wives, my mother again thought to herself:
"My son has not died; now he too shall take a wife!
She wept and lamented, causing me further distress.
"Furthermore, for the fifth time, he has become my son in this present life and left home to study the Way.
My mother weeps daily, saying:
'I have lost my son; I know not where he is. Starving, cold, or facing death, I shall never see him again!'"
"Alas, how bitter and sorrowful! I think of myself:
'Now these five mothers have gathered together, each speaking of her lost son, weeping as they face one another.
I shall become the soul and spirit of one person, acting as a son to these five mothers, so that the five mothers may weep and think of me.'"
"It is for this reason that I smile.
People of the world do not know of rebirth in future lives; they speak only of death.
Yet, when a person performs good, they naturally receive its blessing; when they commit evil, they naturally incur its calamity."
While people are in this world, they indulge themselves in joy and anger without any sense of dread or aversion.
Later, when their suffering becomes unspeakable and they enter the evil realms, it will be too late for regret.
"Because I am weary of the world, I have left my parents to seek the Way.
I regard hell, the animal realm, the hungry ghosts, and poverty as more terrifying than they are."
I have received the kindness of my teacher and accepted the Buddha’s sutras and precepts; I am now liberated and delivered.
I reflect that these five mothers of mine cannot attain liberation, yet they instead worry about my former body.
That which I have desired is already complete.
The people of the world lament for one another in succession, never ceasing their weeping.

The body is merely a tool; the soul departs into emptiness, following the deeds it has performed, unable to sever itself from them. Only by uprooting its very foundation can one attain liberation; yet they only accumulate evil day by day—this is the work of delusion.
"I shall no longer associate with the company of birth and death; like a man who does not sow seeds, I shall only pursue *nirvāṇa*, for *nirvāṇa* is bliss.
Having spoken these words to his teacher, he prostrated before him and then flew away.
The Sutra of the Five Mothers and Sons
